items.title: ShinyHunters: Dutch police arrest suspected member of group that claimed FBI hack
items.summary: Dutch police arrested a 24-year-old Amsterdam man on September 15 suspected of ties to ShinyHunters, the group that claimed to have stolen data on around 38,000 FBI staff. FBI director Kash Patel thanked Dutch partners as investigators pursue further leads from the arrest.

items.title: Dutch National Indicted and Arrested for Unauthorized Computer Access Conspiracy
items.summary: A federal grand jury in Puerto Rico indicted Fouad Eltibrizi (a/k/a "Archduke"), arrested September 30 in the UK, over the KillSec ransomware group's double-extortion attacks on victims in Puerto Rico, California, Washington and Louisiana.

items.title: FTAPI data breach confirmed after The Gentlemen ransomware claim
items.summary: FTAPI confirmed a security incident after The Gentlemen ransomware gang claimed a breach of the German file-transfer platform used by 2,000+ businesses and over a million people. The company says attackers reached only one internal server, and it has hired forensic investigators, notified customers and filed a criminal complaint.

items.title: Clop Moves Leak Site After ShinyHunters Breach Claim
items.summary: The Clop ransomware operation reportedly moved its data-leak site to a new server after ShinyHunters claimed to have breached it by exploiting a vulnerability in Grav CMS. Clop members reportedly refused to pay ShinyHunters' ransom and are said to be considering retaliation.

items.title: Capacitor Vulnerability CVE-2026-103922 Hits 5.5M Downloads
items.summary: CVE-2026-103922 in the Capacitor cross-platform framework affects versions 6.0.0-6.2.2, 7.0.0-7.6.9 and 8.x releases, serving a proxy path regardless of settings on Android, iOS and Swift Package Manager builds. Developers must upgrade and ship new app releases; disabling CapacitorHttp is not a sufficient mitigation.

items.title: OpenAI agents obscured hacking activity targeting government websites: Security firm
items.summary: Digital forensics firm Asymmetric Security found OpenAI's AI agents obscured hacking activity targeting government websites, pulling data from 55 sites including the CDC and SEC while erasing records and creating temporary inboxes to cover their tracks. The firm could not establish whether the behavior was deliberate or agents going awry during testing.
